access_approve_consequence: A RoleBinding granting {subject} the {capability} role is created in namespace {namespace}, with your identity. It covers every Cluster of {namespace}.
access_cap_operator_hint: view, plus backups, restarts, switchovers and pgAdmin
access_cap_viewer_hint: status, events, diagnostics, history and logs
access_deny_consequence: The request of {subject} in {namespace} is closed without a grant; your note is shown to them.
access_expiry_hint: Without an expiry the grant lasts until it is revoked.
access_for_you: The request names you (your user as the API server knows it).
access_intro: Ask for access to the Clusters of a namespace, follow your requests and, where you may create RoleBindings, decide the requests of others. Nobody decides a request that names them. Every decision is a Kubernetes object written with the decider's identity.
access_namespace_wide: An approval binds a role for every Cluster of namespace {namespace}: a RoleBinding cannot be narrowed to one Cluster. Naming a Cluster only tells the reviewer what you need.
access_not_observed: The operator has not reported on this request yet.
access_note_hint: Shown to the person the request names.
access_nothing_to_request: This console offers nothing to request in the namespaces you can see.
access_partial: In {namespaces} you may not list every request: only those naming you are shown.
access_read_only: This console does not write (operations are switched off): requests are shown, nothing can be requested or decided here.
access_request_link: Request more access to this Cluster
access_revoke_consequence: The RoleBinding granting {subject} access in namespace {namespace} is deleted with your identity; the API server refuses their next request.
access_sent: Request sent: it waits for review. Nothing is granted until a reviewer approves it.
access_unchecked: {count} requests were left out: the API server could not be asked whether you may see them. Retry later.
access_withdraw_consequence: Your request in {namespace} is closed without a grant (a denial you make yourself); your note is kept with it.

preview_title: What this change sets in motion
preview_unverified: Unverified: PostgreSQL {major} or CloudNativePG {minor} is not covered by the tables this preview reads. Check the CloudNativePG documentation before relying on it.
preview_unknown: {count} change(s) could not be classified: their effect is unknown.
preview_summary_none: nothing restarts and no configuration is reloaded.
preview_summary_reload: PostgreSQL reloads its configuration on every instance; no instance restarts.
preview_summary_restart: PostgreSQL must restart: each replica's Pod is recreated on its volumes, one at a time, and the primary goes last as shown below.
preview_summary_rollout: every instance's Pod is recreated, one at a time, in the order below.
preview_summary_major_upgrade: the Cluster is shut down and upgraded to a new PostgreSQL major version.
preview_summary_unknown: the effect could not be determined.
preview_strategy_supervised: the operator waits for a person before touching the primary
preview_strategy_unsupervised: the operator updates the primary on its own
preview_steps_by_role: A stored revision holds the spec only: instance names are the Cluster's at the time of the update, so the order is given by role.
preview_action_switchover: switchover to the most advanced replica, then the former primary restarts
preview_action_wait_for_user: waits for a person (supervised): nothing happens until a switchover or restart is requested
preview_action_restart_first: restarts first, by its own instance manager (a lower hot-standby-sensitive value), then the replicas follow
preview_decrease: Lower value of a hot-standby-sensitive setting: the primary restarts first (under supervised, once a person acts), then the replicas.
preview_note: Go's reading of this revision against CloudNativePG's rules; what actually happens is on the timeline and in the Events.
digest_intro: One digest a day per console: what happened on each Cluster you may get during 24 hours. Each digest has its own page, the link delivered messages carry.
digest_not_persistent: in memory: lost when the console restarts
digest_partial_not_observed: The console's memory begins after the window did.
digest_partial_console_restarted: The console was down during the window.
digest_partial_source_gap: A source the timeline rests on was not live during the window.
digest_partial_clusters_unreadable: A namespace's Clusters cannot be read: they are not in this digest.
digest_partial_no_timeline: There is no timeline to read.
digest_late: Made late (a catch-up): health and attention are as of {at}, not as of the end of the window.
digest_partial: Partial: the console did not observe all of these 24 hours, so this is not an all-clear. What happened then may be missing, or placed between two observations.
digest_none: No digest yet: the first one closes at the next scheduled hour.
digest_disabled_detail: This console does not build daily digests (DIGEST_ENABLED=false).
digest_visibility_note: Each digest shows only the Clusters you may get; counts are yours, not the whole console's.
digest_hidden: {count} Cluster(s) you may not see are left out.
digest_console_gaps_note: Times the console itself was not observing: nothing on any Cluster was seen live then.
digest_no_clusters: No Cluster you may get was watched during these 24 hours.
digest_cluster_truncated: Only the most recent entries of this Cluster are listed; its timeline has the rest.
digest_cluster_quiet: Nothing happened on this Cluster in these 24 hours.
preview_summary_start: PostgreSQL starts again on the instances that were stopped (a fence lifted, or hibernation switched off).
preview_summary_shutdown: PostgreSQL stops on the instances below (fencing or hibernation) and stays down until that is lifted.
preview_unknown_no_floor: None of the classified changes restarts anything, but a restart cannot be ruled out.
preview_unknown_floor_note: What is known already does this; the unclassified change(s) may do more.
preview_action_unknown: cannot be said: a change could not be classified
preview_context_absent: not in this PostgreSQL major (PostgreSQL rejects the configuration)
preview_reason_managed_extension: extension library added to or removed from shared_preload_libraries by the operator
forecast_filesystem_autogrow: This is the current filesystem: autoGrow should grow the PVC before then. If it cannot (expansion refused, maxSize reached, archiving failing), PostgreSQL stops writing here.
forecast_full_now_autogrow_set: autoGrow is set but did not grow this filesystem in time: check the VolumeExpansionRefused and VolumeAutoGrowStopped conditions.
forecast_inodes_total_changed: No inode forecast: the inode total changed over the window (XFS allocates inodes on demand), so there is no fixed limit to run toward.
forecast_resized_levelled: The volume was resized at {at}: the readings before it were shifted by the jump the resize made, as it adds reserved blocks counted as used.
forecast_resized_since: The volume was resized at {at}: the fit uses only the readings since then, as a resize shifts the space counted as used by the reserved blocks it adds.
answer_caveats: What this answer does not prove:
answer_gap: In a hole of the window
answer_reported: Only reported by the operator, not verified

assumption_segment_names: WAL continuity, judged from segment names only
assumption_timeline_history: timeline switches, read from the timeline history metadata only

forecast_no_data_inodes: Inode counts are not reported by this filesystem.
forecast_no_volumes: No volume has been trended yet.
forecast_not_growing: Not growing: less than {min} over the last {hours} h.

assistant_not_served_title: This console does not serve AI assistants.
assistant_not_served_admin: The console's administrator turns it on (MCP_ENABLED, or mcp.enabled in the chart); until then there is nothing to connect.
assistant_connected_intro: The assistants you approved on this console. Each acts as you: it sees and does only what you may. The name is the one the application gave itself; the console cannot verify it.
assistant_revoked: {client} is disconnected: every replica refuses its tokens within about a second.
assistant_connected_empty: No assistant is connected as you.
assistant_connected_empty_hint: Connect one with the setup below; it appears here once you approve it.
assistant_disconnect_consequence: Its access and refresh tokens stop working on every replica of this console within about a second. To use it again, connect it again and approve it.
assistant_disconnect_recorded: Performed as {actor}; the console's audit log records it (mcp.revoke).
assistant_access_read_detail: A connected assistant reads what the console shows you (status, replication, backups, storage, diagnostics, insight). It cannot change anything.
assistant_access_operate_detail: The write tools are on: an assistant you approve with "Read and operate" on the consent page (it proposes read-only first) can also request the operations you may request (backup, restart, switchover…), each confirmed in the assistant and recorded in the audit logs.
assistant_access_as_you: It acts as you, through the same authorization as these pages, and never holds more rights than you.
assistant_no_clients: The console offered no client setup.
assistant_step_add_or_file: Or put it in a configuration file (merge into an existing file):
assistant_step_add_file_only: This client has no add command: put it in its configuration file (merge into an existing file).
assistant_step_sign_in_automatic: The client starts the sign-in by itself the first time it calls the console.
assistant_step_consent: Your browser opens this console: sign in if you are not, then approve the consent page. The connection then appears under Connected assistants.
assistant_pack_intro: The prompt pack tells the assistant what the tools are, that text from the cluster is data and not instructions, and to cite the console page of each finding.
assistant_pack_merge: Add it as a section of an existing AGENTS.md; do not replace the file.
assistant_disconnect_all_consequence: Every assistant connected as you stops working on every replica of this console within about a second. Your browser session stays. To use one again, connect it again and approve it.
assistant_disconnect_all_recorded: Performed as {actor}; the console's audit log records each one (mcp.revoke).
assistant_revoked_all: Every assistant is disconnected: every replica refuses their tokens within about a second.
pgbr_failed: pgBackRest recorded it with an error
pgbr_stanza_from_agent: named by the Stanza object; the evidence agent reports it
pgbr_archive_stanza: WAL stanza (split from the backup stanza)
pgbr_window_to: To: last contiguous WAL segment received
pgbr_window_none: No backup reaches the WAL frontier: the agent reports no recovery window for this stanza.
pgbr_retention_unset: not set: pgBackRest never expires a full backup
pgbr_retention_none: The agent was given no retention: the stanza is not compared with one.
pgbr_findings_truncated: The agent cut its findings list: more exist.
pgbr_backups_truncated: Only the newest backups are listed.
backup_predates_cluster_hint: Created before this Cluster, or owned by another Cluster of the same name: not counted in its recency, topology or timeline.
backup_overdue_schedule: overdue: a scheduled run was missed
backup_overdue_default: overdue: older than 7 days, and no backup cadence is known
backup_no_cadence_known: no backup cadence known: warning after 7 days
drill_checks_not_kept: Finished before the console restarted: its outcome and times were kept, its checks were not.
not_restore_tested: Not restore-tested: no restore drill of this Cluster passed in the last {days} days.
pitr_edge_hint_archiver: The newest restore point is uncertain. On the primary, check what PostgreSQL last archived:
pitr_edge_hint_switch: Then force a WAL switch on the primary, so the current segment is archived, and refresh the evidence:
rp_segment_reported: Reported by {source}; not verified against the repository.
rp_segment_covered: Structurally covered: base backup {id} and contiguous archived WAL.
rp_segment_covered_cut: Covered by the paths read, but the collection was cut: a newer timeline may change where a restore goes.
rp_segment_near_hole: Within {margin} of a hole in the archived WAL: segment names cannot place this target on either side.
rp_segment_missing_wal: WAL is missing from the repository: no restore target in this span.
rp_segment_candidate_gap: A WAL gap seen by one scan, not yet confirmed by a second.
rp_segment_continuation_unknown: The evidence cannot tell whether WAL continues here.
rp_segment_near_end: Within {margin} of the end of the archived WAL: segment names cannot tell whether this target's WAL is archived yet.
rp_segment_near_end_no_timeout: Near the end of the archived WAL with archive_timeout disabled: nothing bounds how old the newest archived commit is.
rp_segment_archiving_failed: WAL archiving failed at {failed}: WAL that reaches the repository after a failure holds older commits than its arrival time says, so the arrival time overstates how recent a restore can be.
rp_segment_purge_edge: Within {margin} of the oldest restore point: a retention purge since the repository was last read may have removed this base backup.
rp_segment_missing_after_latest: WAL is missing from the repository after the latest restore point.
rp_segment_collection_cut: The recovery path collection was cut at a bound: newer coverage may exist.
rp_segment_evidence_stale: The repository evidence is stale: newer WAL may have reached the repository since.
rp_segment_after_last_read: Not in the repository when it was last read ({scanned}): WAL archived since may cover this time.
rp_segment_after_frontier: After the newest archived WAL the evidence shows: WAL archived since may cover this time.
rp_tail_prefix_operator: After the last base backup the operator reports ({end}): the operator does not report the archived WAL beyond it.
rp_tail_prefix_evidence: After the end of the window the evidence agent reported ({end}): without the agent's recovery paths the console cannot place this time.
rp_tail_report_age: its own report on /pg/status, read {age} ago
rp_tail_before_archived: WAL archiving is healthy and the primary last archived a segment at {archived}, after this time ({report}): a restore to this time may well be possible; deploy an evidence agent to place it.
rp_tail_before_archived_failing: The primary last archived a segment at {archived}, after this time ({report}), but WAL archiving is failing: this time's WAL may be in the repository; deploy an evidence agent to place it.
rp_tail_before_archived_unconfirmed: The primary last archived a segment at {archived}, after this time ({report}), but WAL archiving is not confirmed healthy: this time's WAL may be in the repository; deploy an evidence agent to place it.
rp_tail_after_archived: This time is after the primary's last archived segment ({archived}, {report}): its WAL may still be only on the primary.
rp_tail_after_archived_failing: WAL archiving is failing: WAL after the primary's last archived segment ({archived}, {report}) is likely not in the repository.
rp_tail_archived_unknown: The primary's last archived WAL time is not known (its /pg/status was not read, or it reports none): the console cannot say whether this time's WAL reached the repository; deploy an evidence agent to place it.
rp_tail_archived_unknown_failing: WAL archiving is failing and the primary's last archived WAL time is not known: this time's WAL is likely not in the repository.
rp_check_no_window: No restore window is known for this cluster: {reason}.
rp_check_before_earliest_cut: Before the earliest restore point the evidence shows ({earliest}), but the collections were cut: an older backup may exist.
rp_check_before_earliest: Before the earliest restore point ({earliest}): no base backup that old is in the repository.
rp_check_before_earliest_reported: Before the earliest restore point ({earliest}): no base backup that old is reported.
rp_check_reported: Inside the window the operator reports ({source}); no repository evidence confirms it.
rp_check_reported_by_agent: Inside the window the evidence agent reports ({source}); its recovery paths do not confirm it.
rp_check_covered: Structurally covered: restore from base backup {id} and replay the archived WAL to this time.
rp_check_not_placed: The evidence does not place this time.
rp_caveat_segment_names: Judged from WAL segment names in the repository: the WAL bytes were not read and no restore was run.
rp_caveat_latest_bounded: The latest restore point is bounded by when the last contiguous segment reached the repository; the newest transactions may still be only on the instance.
rp_caveat_collections_cut: The evidence collections were cut at a bound: a span shown as not covered may be covered.
rp_caveat_archiving_failing: WAL archiving is failing: the newest WAL is on the instance, not in the repository.
rp_caveat_archiving_failing_since: WAL archiving is failing: the primary last archived a segment at {archived}; newer WAL is on the instance, not in the repository.
answer_reported_agent: Only in the evidence agent's window, not confirmed by its recovery paths
span_reported_agent: reported by the evidence agent, not confirmed by recovery paths
pitr_edge_hint_switch_reported: Then force a WAL switch on the primary, so the current segment is archived, and check pg_stat_archiver again:
rp_segment_wal_end: WAL ends near here: the newest archived segment reached the repository at {end}, and its last commit may be up to {margin} older. A recovery_target_time after the last commit fails with "recovery ended before configured recovery target was reached"; to restore everything archived, restore to the end of WAL (no recovery target).
rp_segment_archive_backlog: {segments} WAL segments are waiting to be archived on the primary, since before the sweeps the console keeps: segments reach the repository late, so the arrival time of the newest overstates how recent a restore can be.
rp_segment_after_last_read_failing: Not in the repository when it was last read ({scanned}), and WAL archiving is failing: this time's WAL is likely not in the repository.
rp_segment_after_frontier_failing: After the newest archived WAL the evidence shows, and WAL archiving is failing: this time's WAL is likely not in the repository.
rp_segment_after_last_read_backlog: Not in the repository when it was last read ({scanned}), and {segments} WAL segments are waiting to be archived on the primary: this time's WAL is likely still only on the primary.
rp_segment_after_frontier_backlog: After the newest archived WAL the evidence shows, and {segments} WAL segments are waiting to be archived on the primary: this time's WAL is likely still only on the primary.
rp_tail_archived_unknown_backlog: {segments} WAL segments are waiting to be archived on the primary and its last archived WAL time is not known: this time's WAL may still be only on the primary.
rp_tail_before_archived_backlog: The primary last archived a segment at {archived}, after this time ({report}), with {segments} segments waiting to be archived: the archiver is behind, so this time's WAL may not be in the repository yet; deploy an evidence agent to place it.
rp_tail_after_archived_backlog: {segments} WAL segments are waiting to be archived on the primary: WAL after its last archived segment ({archived}, {report}) is likely still only on the primary.
rp_reason_backups_cut: the backup collection was cut at a bound: older backups may exist
rp_reason_reported_window: the window is the operator's report, not repository evidence
rp_reason_no_paths: the evidence agent published no recovery paths
rp_reason_no_consistent_path: no recovery path reaches its base backup's consistency point: the evidence cannot place a restore point
rp_reason_paths_stale: the recovery paths could not be read again ({detail}): these are the last good ones
rp_reason_paths_cut: the recovery path collection was cut at a bound: the restore target timeline cannot be told
rp_reason_missing_after_latest: WAL is missing after the latest restore point: recent times are not restorable from the repository
rp_reason_holes: the window has holes where WAL is missing
rp_reason_candidate_gaps: the window has candidate gaps a second scan has not confirmed yet
rp_reason_failed_recently: WAL archiving failed recently: the newest restore points are uncertain
rp_reason_archive_backlog: {segments} WAL segments are waiting to be archived on the primary: the newest restore points are uncertain
rp_reason_orphan_timeline: timeline {timeline} is in the archive but not connected by valid history: a restore cannot follow it
rp_reason_undrawn: some backups have no observed recovery path past their consistency point
rp_check_history_file: The evidence names the timeline history file {file} as missing or unreadable: the coverage shown rests on it.
tl_gap_not_all_read: timeline history files were not all read
tl_reason_history_missing_no_follow: history {timeline} is missing: no restore can follow timeline {timeline}
tl_reason_latest_unknown: the timeline a default restore follows is unknown: {gap}
tl_reason_latest_stops: a default restore (recovery_target_timeline 'latest') stops on timeline {latest}: {gap}; timeline {newest} needs an explicit targetTLI
cap_phase_unverified: phase table not verified for CNPG {minor}: a healthy phase is shown as a warning
cap_phase_undetected: CNPG version not detected: phase read against the CNPG {table} table, so a healthy phase is shown as a warning
cap_condition_unverified: condition table not verified for CNPG {minor}: shown as a warning
cap_condition_undetected: CNPG version not detected: condition read against the CNPG {table} table, so it is shown as a warning
tl_reason_needs_target_sibling: a default restore follows timeline {latest}, whose history does not lead through timeline {timeline}: needs targetTLI {timeline}
tl_reason_ancestry_invalid: timeline ancestry contains missing or invalid evidence
tl_reason_ancestry_invalid_file: timeline ancestry contains missing or invalid evidence: {file}: {problem}
tl_problem_unreadable: timeline history could not be read
tl_problem_range_disagrees: child WAL range disagrees with timeline switchpoint
rp_reason_timeline_not_established: the agent's timeline evidence is {state} ({detail}): no recovery path is shown as coverage until the timeline a default restore follows is established
rp_reason_timeline_not_established_bare: the agent's timeline evidence is {state}: no recovery path is shown as coverage until the timeline a default restore follows is established
rp_reason_agent_predates: the evidence agent is an older build that does not resolve recovery_target_timeline 'latest' as PostgreSQL does: its recovery paths are not shown as coverage; upgrade the agent
rp_off_target_needs_target: Base backup {id} reaches this span on timeline {timeline}, which a default restore (recovery_target_timeline 'latest') does not follow: a restore along it needs targetTLI {timeline} (recovery_target_timeline: '{timeline}').
rp_caveat_timeline_warning_file: The evidence reports the timeline history file {file}, which no default restore reads, as invalid: the coverage shown does not rest on it, but a restore that names its timeline would fail.
rp_caveat_timeline_warning: The evidence reports a timeline history file no default restore reads as invalid ({detail}): the coverage shown does not rest on it, but a restore that names its timeline would fail.
recovery_off_target: Restorable only by naming a timeline
rp_segment_archive_backlog_since: {segments} WAL segments have been waiting to be archived on the primary since {since} or a little before: WAL archived since then reached the repository late, so its arrival time overstates how recent a restore can be.
answer_target_timeline: Default recovery_target_timeline 'latest': a restore that names no timeline follows this one.
